questions.question:
He has ----- red and white horse.
The syeds will establish ---- school after their grandmother's name.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" because "horse" is a singular countable noun, and both "red" and "white" describe the same single animal.

questions.question: He went to ----- and -----.[]
questions.explanation: Most countries take no article (Canada), but countries with "United" or "States" in the name require "the" (the USA).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: The students have gone to see the Himalaya.
The students have gone to see the Himalayas.
The students have gone to see Himalaya.
The students have gone to see Himalayas.
questions.explanation: Use "the" before the names of mountain ranges (plural), like the Himalayas.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: The Padma is longest river in Bangladesh.
The Padma is longest river in the Bangladesh.
Padma is longest river in Bangladesh.
The Padma is the longest river in Bangladesh.
questions.explanation: Use "the" before river names (The Padma) and before superlative adjectives (the longest)

questions.question:
I know he is ----- honest man.
She is ----- unknown woman here.[]
questions.explanation: Use "an" because "honest" begins with a silent 'h' (vowel sound) and "unknown" begins with a vowel sound.

questions.question: I saw ----- beggar.[]
questions.explanation: Although "one" starts with a vowel letter, it sounds like 'w', which is a consonant sound.

questions.question: My mother gave me ----- one-taka note.[]
questions.explanation: "one-taka" starts with the consonant 'w' sound,requiring "a".

questions.question:
Sohana is ----- European lady.
He prefers ----- European country for spending his vacation.
Denmark is ----- European nation.[]
questions.explanation: "European" starts with a 'y' consonant sound, so "a" is used instead of "an".

questions.question: We made ----- fire.[]
questions.explanation: In the phrase "made a fire," it refers to a single instance of a campfire or hearth fire.

questions.question:
The book is ----- one I was seriously looking for.
I found ----- old lady came to our house.[]
questions.explanation: "The" is used because the "one" and the "old lady" are specific—the speaker is identifying a particular person or thing already mentioned or known.

questions.question: He has ----- M.A. from Public University.[]
questions.explanation: The letter 'M' in "M.A." is pronounced starting with a vowel sound "em"

questions.question: The Meghna falls into ----- Bay of Bengal.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" before names of bays, gulfs, and oceans (The Bay of Bengal).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: The Dhaka is on the Buriganga.
questions.explanation: Use "the" before names of rivers. Cities (Dhaka) do not take an article.

questions.question: There is ----- cow in the field.[]
questions.explanation: "Cow" is a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time without specific identification.

questions.question: He received ----- wound.[]
questions.explanation: "Wound" starts with a consonant sound (/w/), so "a" is appropriate for a single injury.

questions.question: Industry is ----- mother of goodluck.[]
questions.explanation: This is a metaphorical title/definition. When "mother" is used to define a specific relationship to a quality (good luck), use "the".

questions.question: Birds of ----- feather flock together.[]
questions.explanation: "Birds of a feather" is a fixed idiom where "a" means "the same."

questions.question: Mr.Robert lives in ----- Hague.[]
questions.explanation: The Hague" is one of the few city names that always includes a definite article as part of its proper name.

questions.question:
My friend holds ----- unique position.
It was ----- unique sight.
This is ----- unique problem.
This is ----- unique opportunity.[]
questions.explanation: Like "European," the word "unique" starts with a 'y' consonant sound, requiring "a".

questions.question: ----- Germans are very enterprising.[]
questions.explanation: When referring to a national group or people as a whole (Germans), use "The".

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
questions.explanation: "Must" is used here as a countable noun meaning "a necessity," so it requires the indefinite article "a".

questions.question:
He is ----- most famous teacher of this college.
Dhaka is ----- biggest city in Bangladesh.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" before superlative adjectives like "most famous" and "biggest."

questions.question: Which one is correct ?[]
questions.explanation: Descriptive geographical names that are plural in form (like The Sundarbans) always take the definite article "the."

questions.question: Tisha has a knack for playing ----- piano.[]
questions.explanation: Both "on piano" (focusing on the activity) and "the piano" (focusing on the instrument) are grammatically acceptable, though "the" is standard for musical instruments.

questions.question: কোনটিতে Article এর সঠিক প্রয়োগ নেই ?[]
questions.explanation: The word "university" starts with a consonant sound, so it should take "a", not "an."

questions.question: Man এর পূর্বে কোন Article বসালে মানবজাতি বোঝায় ?[]
questions.explanation: When "Man" is used to represent the entire human race, no article is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: The Gold is a precious metal.
A Gold is a precious metal.
questions.explanation: Material nouns like "Gold" do not take an article when used in a general sense.

questions.question: None but ----- brave deserves ----- fair.[]
questions.explanation: "The" + adjective (the brave) represents a whole class of people. This is a famous proverb: "None but the brave deserves the fair."

questions.question: I know someone who wrote a book about ----- life of Bangabandhu Sheikh Rahman.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" because "life" is made specific by the phrase "of Bangabandhu Sheikh Rahman."

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: An Omar Khayyam is rarely born.
A Omar Khayyam is rarely born.
The Omar Khayyam is rarely born.
questions.explanation: Use "an" before a proper noun (Omar Khayyam) when comparing someone to a famous person's qualities (meaning "a person like him").

questions.question: Find out the correct sentence.[]
options: The Bangalees are a brave nation.
The Bangalee is a brave nation.
questions.explanation: Use "The" before the names of nations or ethnic groups (The Bangalees) when referring to them collectively.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: A Padma is a big river.
The Padma is a big river.
questions.explanation: Always use "the" before the names of rivers (The Padma).

questions.question: নিচের কোন বাক্যটি শুদ্ধ ?[]
options: A lion is beast of prey
The lion is a beast of prey
The Lion is beast of prey
questions.explanation: "The" + singular common noun (The lion) can represent a whole species.

questions.question: Which is the correct sentence ?[]
questions.explanation: "Virtue" is a countable noun in this context, and "great" starts with a consonant sound, so it requires "a".

questions.question: Find out the correct sentence.[]
options: The nature is looking beautiful in the spring.
Nature looks beautiful in the spring.
The nature looks like beautiful in spring.
The nature is beautiful in spring.
questions.explanation: "Nature" does not take an article when referring to the physical world/environment in a general sense.

questions.question: All applicants must possess -----.[]
questions.explanation: The word "university" starts with a consonant sound, so it should take "a", not "an."

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: He earns hundred taka a day.
He earns a hundred taka a day.
He earned a hundred taka day.
questions.explanation: "A hundred" is the standard way to express the number 100 in a sentence.

questions.question: Choose the right article.[]
options: Who is woman in a red sari ?
Who is the woman in red sari ?
Who is the woman in a red sari ?
Who is the woman in the red sari ?
questions.explanation: "The" is used because the woman is specified by her clothing ("in the red sari").

questions.question: Choose the right article.[]
options: What the chilly day it was !
What a chilly day it was !
What an chilly day it was !
questions.explanation: In exclamatory sentences starting with "What," use "a/an" before a singular countable noun.

questions.question: Sugar is nice in ----- cup of tea.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" to refer to a single, non-specific container (a cup).

questions.question: Man is ----- architect of his own fate.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" because the noun "architect" is made specific by the phrase "of his own fate."

questions.question: The dress was designed by ----- famous Indian artist.[]
questions.explanation: "Famous Indian artist" is a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time without specific identification, so use "a".

questions.question: This is rather ----- difficult question.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" after "rather" when it precedes an adjective and a singular countable noun (rather a difficult question).

questions.question: ----- Iqbal is not born in every age.[]
questions.explanation: Use "an" before a proper noun (Iqbal) when referring to someone with the same qualities as that person (meaning "a person like Iqbal").

questions.question: There is ----- boy on ----- bicycle.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" for the first mention of the boy. Use "the" for "bicycle" because it implies a specific or standard mode of transport in this context.

questions.question:
I want to play ----- guitar.
Adiba is learning to play ----- piano.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" before the names of musical instruments (the guitar, the piano) when speaking about playing them.

questions.question: ----- Actor is the life of a play.[]
questions.explanation: Use "An" before "Actor" (singular countable noun starting with a vowel sound) to represent the entire class/profession in a general statement.

questions.question:
May I ask you ----- question ?
Helen works eight hours ----- day.
Twelve inches make ----- foot.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" for singular countable units: "a question," "a day" (meaning per day), and "a foot" (meaning one foot).

questions.question: George ----- sixth was ----- king of England.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" before ordinal numbers (the sixth) and when a title is followed by a specific country ("the king of England").

questions.question: Do you know the name of ----- artist who painted the portrait ?[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" because the "artist" is specific—the one who painted the portrait.
